newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada wholesale trade falls 0.7 pct in November.
newsitem.headline: Canada wholesale trade falls 0.7 pct in November.

text.p: Canada's wholesale trade fell 0.7 percent seasonally adjusted in November to C$21.70 billion, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
Sales, adj C$21.70 bln -0.7 pct +8.0 pct
Inventories, adj C$31.79 bln +0.8 pct -0.3 pct
Note - dollar figures are billions. Other figures are percentage changes.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 0.8 percent month-on-month rise in November.
StatsCan also revised its figmre for October sales to C$21.86 billion from C$21.94 billion.
The agency said year-to-date sales were almost 4.0 percent higher compared to the same period in 1995.

Six of the 11 trade groups had lower sales in November, led by a 7.6 percent decline in sales of computers, packaged software and other electronic equipment. Wholesale sales of metal, hardware, plumbing and heating equipment dropped 3.0 percent in the month.
The strongest gains in the month were a 2.5 percent increase in wholesale sales of "other products" and a 2.0 percent increase in sales of lumber and building materials.
